name: MITRE ATT&CK Knowledge Base for Network Security Operations

techniques.name: Brute Force: Password Guessing
techniques.description: Adversaries may systematically guess passwords to gain unauthorized access to accounts, attempting multiple combinations on targeted authentication services such as FTP (port 21) or SSH (port 22).
indicators: Rapid sequence of failed authentication attempts within seconds
High volume of small TCP flows to port 21 or 22
Uniform packet length sequences and low backward payload bytes
Multiple SYN packets without successful interactive shell session
techniques.objectives: Obtain valid user credentials to penetrate perimeter access and establish remote shell access.
mitigations: M1036: Account Use Policies - Implement strict account lockout thresholds after 3-5 consecutive failures.
M1032: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) - Require hardware tokens or OTP for all external administrative interfaces.
M1035: Limit Access to Remote Services - Restrict SSH/FTP ingress via VPN or bastion host IP whitelisting.
techniques.detection: Monitor authentication daemon logs (sshd, vsftpd) and detect high-frequency TCP connection flows targeting port 22 or 21 from single or clustered IP addresses.

techniques.name: Network Service Discovery
techniques.description: Adversaries may enumerate open ports and listening services on victim hosts to identify attack surfaces, vulnerable software versions, or misconfigured daemons.
indicators: Rapid sequence of SYN/FIN packets across a wide range of destination ports
Very low Flow Duration (< 50 ms per probe) and negligible payload transfer
RST-ACK packets returned by closed ports or dropped packet timeouts
Asymmetric Down/Up ratio from single source IP across multiple victim sockets
techniques.objectives: Map accessible victim perimeter services prior to vulnerability exploitation or brute-force delivery.
mitigations: M1031: Network Intrusion Prevention - Deploy stateful firewall rules to drop unsolicited port probe sweeps.
M1037: Filter Network Traffic - Close all non-essential perimeter ports; restrict administrative ports.
M1050: Exploit Protection - Minimize banner exposure and disable verbose error responses.
techniques.detection: Correlate sliding windows where a single source IP contacts > 15 distinct destination ports within a 10-second interval.

techniques.name: Network Denial of Service: Direct Network Flood
techniques.description: Adversaries may direct high volumes of network traffic toward an architecture to exhaust network bandwidth or saturate state tables on perimeter firewalls and routers.
indicators: Abnormal surge in Flow Packets/s exceeding 10,000 pps
Extreme ratio of Forward Packets to Backward Packets
High concentration of TCP SYN or UDP datagram floods from distributed IP sources
Service degradation, dropped connections, and packet loss on victim edge router
techniques.objectives: Disrupt legitimate operational availability and deny service access to customers and employees.
mitigations: M1037: Filter Network Traffic - Implement upstream upstream BGP Anycast and ISP null-routing (blackholing).
M1021: Restrict Web-Based Content - Deploy DDoS mitigation proxies (Cloudflare, Akamai, AWS Shield).
M1031: Network Intrusion Prevention - Configure SYN cookies and TCP half-open connection rate limiting.
techniques.detection: Detect volumetric anomalies where aggregate incoming packet rates across an IP subnet exceed baseline thresholds by 300% within a 5-second tumbling window.

techniques.name: Endpoint Denial of Service: Application Exhaustion Flood
techniques.description: Adversaries may exhaust software resources on web servers using asymmetric application-layer attacks like Slowloris, Slowhttptest, or GoldenEye by holding HTTP connections open with partial headers.
indicators: Very long Flow Duration (> 60-120 seconds per session)
Low packet rate per session with periodic keep-alive byte transfers
Maxed-out web server thread pool (Apache MaxRequestWorkers / Nginx worker_connections)
504 Gateway Timeout or 503 Service Unavailable errors on web application
techniques.objectives: Consume all server worker threads or sockets without triggering bandwidth-based volumetric volumetric alert thresholds.
mitigations: M1037: Filter Network Traffic - Configure aggressive HTTP connection and request header timeout limits.
M1050: Exploit Protection - Deploy reverse proxy with asynchronous non-blocking connection handling (e.g., Nginx, HAProxy).
M1021: Restrict Web-Based Content - Set client body buffer limits and minimum data transfer rates.
techniques.detection: Identify connections with abnormally high Flow Duration combined with minimal bytes/second and incomplete HTTP request termination.

techniques.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
techniques.description: Adversaries may attempt to exploit vulnerabilities, bugs, or input validation flaws in public web applications (such as SQL Injection, Cross-Site Scripting, or Command Injection) to execute unauthorized commands.
indicators: HTTP requests targeting ports 80 or 443 with unusual URI parameter lengths or special characters
Repetitive POST/GET requests targeting form endpoints or database query parameters
High variance in backward packet length indicating database error disclosures
Subflow payload signatures containing SQL escape sequences or script tags
techniques.objectives: Extract sensitive database records, execute arbitrary code, or hijack authenticated user sessions.
mitigations: M1050: Exploit Protection - Deploy a Web Application Firewall (WAF) with OWASP Core Rule Set.
M1016: Vulnerability Scanning - Run regular dynamic and static code security assessments.
M1041: Defensive Software Development - Use parameterized queries and output sanitization.
techniques.detection: Monitor web server request logs and WAF alerts for SQL query syntax, script injections, and abnormal status codes (500 Internal Error, 200 with database dumps).

techniques.name: Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols (Command and Control)
techniques.description: Adversaries may communicate using application layer protocols (e.g., HTTP/HTTPS or IRC) to avoid network filtering and control compromised botnet zombie nodes or implants.
indicators: Periodic beaconing intervals between internal endpoint and external C2 host
Persistent TCP sessions with uniform Flow IAT (Inter-Arrival Time) patterns
Encrypted or obfuscated payloads on port 8080, 6667, or 443
Simultaneous outgoing connections to identical external IPs from multiple internal hosts
techniques.objectives: Maintain operational control, receive instructions, exfiltrate data, and stage synchronized secondary attacks.
mitigations: M1037: Filter Network Traffic - Restrict outbound egress traffic using strict proxy authentication.
M1020: SSL/TLS Inspection - Inspect TLS traffic for anomalous certificate authorities and C2 beaconing.
M1049: Antivirus/Antimalware - Block known botnet binary execution via EDR endpoint containment.
techniques.detection: Detect regular, rhythmic communication patterns (low Flow IAT Variance) directed to external unclassified IP addresses.

techniques.name: Exploitation of Remote Services
techniques.description: Adversaries may exploit vulnerabilities in remote services (such as SMB, RDP, or SSH) to move laterally across an internal network after initial breach.
indicators: Internal workstation initiating SMB (port 445) or RPC traffic to multiple peer workstations
High volume of bidirectional data transfers following port reconnaissance
Abnormal process creation triggered by incoming network sockets
Elevated privileges gained on secondary internal subnet machines
techniques.objectives: Expand access across victim subnets, locate high-value target assets, and establish persistence.
mitigations: M1030: Network Segmentation - Segment internal subnets with VLANs and microsegmentation firewalls.
M1026: Privileged Account Management - Disable local administrator credential reuse across workstations (LAPS).
M1051: Patch Management - Rapidly apply security patches to internal enterprise service daemons.
techniques.detection: Correlate internal workstation IP initiating outbound service connections to other workstations on ports 445/139/3389.
